newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher - No German rate move needed.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher - No German rate move needed.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Thursday that a move in German interest rates was neither foreseeable nor necessary.
Asked whether an interest rate increase was needed to strengthen the mark, Kuehbacher told Reuters: "We do not need to strengthen the mark."
Speaking after a speech given by state secretary to the finance ministry Juergen Stark in Berlin, the central bank council member also said the recent movements in the dollar were "not sensational".
Kuehbacher added that any interest rate movement in Germany was "not foreseeable".
He also said that the German government's forecast for 2.5 percent growth in 1997 was pitched too high.
"Growth of 2.5 percent is longer achievable," he said. "The council of economic advisers will have to scale down this forecast."
